response: HTTP/2 reduces application-level head-of-line blocking through multiplexed streams, but TCP still has transport-level head-of-line blocking: a lost packet can delay all streams sharing that connection. HTTP/3 runs over QUIC, where streams can progress independently after unrelated packet loss, and it also improves connection migration (useful when networks change). If your users see meaningful packet loss or mobile-network changes, HTTP/3 can help; on stable, low-loss networks, HTTP/2 may be entirely sufficient.
